# Sparrow

Sparrow draws charts in the browser from a plain data array and about six lines of config. 14 kB gzipped, no runtime dependencies.

Most charting libraries make you pick a side. The small ones give you a line chart and a bar chart, then run out of road the first time a designer asks for a second y-axis. The big ones handle that fine, but you pay 300 kB and inherit a plugin system, a theme system, and an API that has been backward compatible since 2014. Sparrow aims at the middle — enough primitives to build the chart you were actually asked for, few enough concepts to keep in your head.

The core is three things: a scale, a mark, an axis. Every built-in chart type is composed from those, in ordinary readable code. The line chart is about 40 lines. When the built-in you want doesn't exist, you write it the same way we did.

Rendering is SVG by default, with a canvas backend for anything past a few thousand points. React, Vue and Svelte wrappers live in this repo and are thin on purpose.

Sparrow is alpha. The API will change before 1.0.
